text_simplified: With weakness of religion and media focus on corrupting women, clothing not befitting Muslim women has spread, so a young girl grows up exposing her body until that becomes normal for her when she grows older. The Muslim woman is distinguished by modest, covering attire. The author mentions the hadith of 'women who are clothed yet naked.' Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) explained that 'clothed yet naked' refers to wearing garments that are transparent, short, or tight. Shaykh Ibn Baz (may Allah have mercy on him) emphasized that it is not permissible to be lax in dressing young girls in short clothes, because raising them upon that leads them to grow accustomed to it when they get older.

review_defects.why: The English reverses the order of the first two sentences, placing the general principle (Muslim woman distinguished by modest attire) after the problem statement, whereas the Arabic opens with it.
The English adds the honorific '(may Allah have mercy on him)' for both scholars, which is not present in the Arabic for either.
